title: Anonymous Function
body:
```js
const foo = function() { ... }
```
A function with no name of its own. It is a value like any other, so it can be assigned to a
variable, passed as an argument, or returned.

The reason to want one: if a function is only used in one place, giving it a name adds an
identifier to the scope that nothing else needs. That is the whole argument in
[[Call Back Function]]:

```js
function displayPopup() { alert("Hello!"); }
setTimeout(displayPopup, 200);              // named, and now displayPopup is in scope forever

setTimeout(function () { alert("Hello!"); }, 200);   // anonymous
setTimeout(() => alert("Hello!"), 200);              // anonymous, arrow
```

The catch is debugging: an anonymous function shows up as `<anonymous>` in a stack trace,
which is worse than a name when something throws. Modern engines infer a name from the
variable it was assigned to, so `const foo = function () {}` reports as `foo`, but one passed
straight into an argument list has nothing to infer from.

Unlike a declaration, an anonymous function expression is not usefully [[Hoisting|hoisted]].
See [[JS Functions]], [[Arrow Syntax]], and [[Nested Function]].
